title: Monthly Growth Credits on LESA Balances
content:
On plans of Set-Aside Accounts whose balance grows, the undisbursed balance grows monthly at an annual rate equal to the HECM loan's note rate in effect for the month plus the plan's growth spread; the credit records that annual rate as the rate applied.

## How a month's growth is credited

- Growth for a month is credited on the plan's posting day of the following month, recorded against that month.
- It is computed on the set-aside balance at the end of the month: that balance times the annual rate in percent, divided by twelve hundred (one twelfth of the annual rate applied to the balance), rounded half up to the cent as the plan's rounding rule sets.
- Growth is credited only while the set-aside status is active.
- A month whose ending balance is 0.00 posts nothing.
- Repair Set-Aside, Servicing Fee Set-Aside and Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve balances never grow.
- Each growth month is credited at most once.

## Worked example on hypothetical figures

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Balance at the end of March | 10,000.00 |
| Note rate in effect for March | 6.25 percent |
| Growth spread (as in the plan schedule for the growing plans) | 0.5 percentage points |
| Annual rate applied | 6.75 percent |
| Growth for March | 10,000.00 times 6.75, divided by 1,200, which is 56.25 |
| Credited | On the posting day of April, recorded against March |

A second hypothetical month: an ending balance of 3,333.33 at 6.75 percent gives 18.7499..., rounded half up to the cent as 18.75.
